study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: R. Bhome et al., NeuroImage: Clinical, 2024
study_identification_part.si_4_title: A neuroimaging measure to capture heterogeneous patterns of atrophy in Parkinson's disease and dementia with Lewy bodies

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study utilized patient and control data from University College London (UCL) and the National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center (NACC). It also applied a pre-trained normative model developed by Rutherford et al. (2022) using a large reference cohort.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: We included 108 participants with PD (all from the UCL site); and 61 people with DLB (36 from UCL, 25 from the NACC site), plus 165 controls (38 from UCL, 127 from NACC)... Their reference cohort comprised 58,836 participants from 82 sites.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Bhome2024.pdf.md: 2.1 Participants, 2.4 Reference normative dataset, 3.1 Participants

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Control data from UCL (n=38) and NACC (n=127) were used to recalibrate the pre-trained normative model (Rutherford 2022) to the study sites. PD and DLB participants from these sites were then compared against the recalibrated model.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: The reference normative model was recalibrated to the study datasets with an adapted transfer learning approach (Kia et al., 2022). This involved inputting control data from our two study sites into the reference normative model... Z-scores were then generated for each individual with DLB or PD
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Bhome2024.pdf.md: 2.5 Applying neuroimaging normative modelling to study data

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: Model-1 is a structural normative model (Bayesian Linear Regression) built on a reference cohort of 58,836 healthy participants (train-phase). It was recalibrated for this study using 165 additional controls (38 UCL, 127 NACC), bringing the overall healthy control count to 59,001.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: Their reference cohort comprised 58,836 participants from 82 sites... plus 165 controls (38 from UCL, 127 from NACC), used to calibrate the reference dataset models

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The normative model used is a lifespan model (Rutherford et al. 2022), typically covering ages 2 to 100. Specific mean and SD for the combined cohort of 59,001 or the recalibration controls are not explicitly reported in the text or tables. Inclusion criteria for UCL controls were aged 50-80.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: Rutherford and colleagues (Rutherford et al., 2022) modelled normative lifespan curves... Inclusion criteria were being aged 50 -80 [for UCL controls]

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The normative model (Rutherford et al. 2022) was developed using age and sex as covariates, but specific sex counts or percentages for the 58,836 reference cohort or the 165 recalibration controls are not provided in the manuscript.
dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: Rutherford and colleagues (Rutherford et al., 2022) modelled normative lifespan curves ... with age and sex as covariates
